item.title: Marrickville, Burwood and Rouse Hill Medicare Urgent Care Clinics now open
item.content:
The Albanese Government is delivering three new Medicare Urgent Care Clinics, all now open in Marrickville, Burwood and Rouse Hill.

The clinics offer walk-in care for urgent but non-life-threatening conditions and patients will be fully bulk billed. The clinics are open seven days a week, and all operate for extended hours:

  • The Marrickville Medicare Urgent Care Clinic is located at 14 Rich St, Marrickville, open 8am – 10pm
  • The Burwood Medicare Urgent Care Clinic is located at shop G01/8 Elsie Street, Burwood open 8am – 10pm
  • The Rouse Hill Medicare Urgent Care Clinic is located at Level 1,10-14 Market Lane, Rouse Hill, open 8am – 8pm

The Medicare Urgent Care Clinics will help to ease pressure on NSW local hospitals where around 30 per cent of presentations in 2023-24 were for semi-urgent or non-urgent conditions.

New data from the NSW Bureau of Health shows the Albanese Government’s Medicare Urgent Care Clinics across New South Wales are easing pressure on NSW hospitals. Semi-urgent presentations to NSW emergency departments have dropped by 5.1 per cent while non-urgent presentations have dropped by 8.7 per cent.

Nationally, Medicare Urgent Care Clinics have seen more than 2.2 million presentations since the first sites opened in June 2023 and across New South Wales there have been over 452,000 presentations.

The Medicare Urgent Care Clinics were selected to operate following a competitive tender process led by local Primary Health Networks.

Quotes attributable to Prime Minister

“Medicare Urgent Care Clinics help patients get the care they need and ease pressure on hospitals.

“I’m so pleased the Inner West will join communities across the country able to access free, walk-in medical help for urgent but non-life-threatening conditions.

“Labor is building Australia’s future with the largest investment in Medicare in over 40 years.

“Once all of Labor’s clinics are open, four in five Australians will live within a 20-minute drive of a bulk billed Medicare Urgent Care Clinic.”

Quotes attributable to Minister Butler

“We’re delivering on our promise to open more Medicare Urgent Care Clinics in Sydney.

“These three new clinics across Sydney will be open seven days a week, for extended hours and most importantly patients will be fully bulk billed.

“This new data shows Medicare Urgent Care Clinics are taking the pressure off New South Wales hospitals and making sure patients can get the care they need when they need it.”

Quotes attributable to the Attorney-General and Member for Greenway, Hon Michelle Rowland MP

“I promised to deliver a Medicare Urgent Care Clinic for our community – and now, that promise is a reality.

“The Albanese Government is delivering the critical services North West Sydney deserves.

“This clinic will make a real difference for locals by providing convenient, urgent treatment free of charge – all you will need is your Medicare card.

“This would not have been possible without the support of our local community, who fought hard to secure a Medicare Urgent Care Clinic close to home.

“This is a huge win for our local health system, with the new Medicare Urgent Care Clinic taking pressure off the emergency department at Blacktown Hospital.”

Quotes attributable to Sally Sitou MP, Member for Reid

“I promised our community we would deliver a Medicare Urgent Care Clinic in Burwood – and now, that promise is a reality.

“This clinic will make a real difference for locals by providing convenient, bulk billed urgent care right here in the heart of Burwood.

“The opening of the clinic is a huge win for our community, taking the pressure off the emergency department at Concord Repatriation Hospital.”
